sources.snippet: Broan-NuTone F40000 Series: 30-inch undercabinet hood, painted steel body in white/black/bisque/stainless look, aluminum mesh filters, incandescent lighting (2x 40W bulbs), 2-speed rocker switch control. 210 CFM rated. 6-inch round duct connection. 1-year limited warranty. ~$60 retail.

Industry standard for range ventilation is minimum 100 CFM per linear foot of range width. A 30-inch (2.5 foot) range requires minimum 250 CFM for adequate ventilation during normal cooking. The Broan F40000 at 210 CFM falls below this minimum threshold. During high-heat cooking (frying, searing, wok), ventilation effectiveness is significantly compromised. Indoor air quality studies show that inadequate kitchen ventilation allows NO2, CO, and PM2.5 to accumulate to levels exceeding outdoor air quality standards.
sources.classification_reason: Building science evidence that 210 CFM is objectively inadequate for intended use

sources.snippet: Repair technicians describe builder-grade hoods like the F40000 as 'disposable appliances.' Motor life is typically 5-8 years. Axial fan design is louder and moves less air than centrifugal at equivalent noise. At 6.5 sones, owners frequently don't use the hood because it's too loud — which defeats the ventilation purpose entirely. Replacement cost ($60-80 for whole unit) often makes more sense than repair ($40-60 for motor + labor).
sources.classification_reason: Repair tech consensus confirming disposable product category

sources.snippet: Professional installers and designers universally consider the F40000-class hood as the absolute floor of residential ventilation. Quote: 'Builders install these because code requires a hood, not because this provides adequate ventilation.' Painted steel body discolors and chips in kitchen environment. Mesh filters clog within weeks if the homeowner actually cooks. Incandescent lights burn out frequently and add heat. The only advantage is universal availability and instant replaceability.
sources.classification_reason: Professional consensus on absolute floor positioning

sources.snippet: Broan F40000 series listed in HVI certified products directory. CFM and sone ratings independently verified.
sources.classification_reason: Independent performance verification — confirms 210 CFM is the actual rating

sources.snippet: Numerous homeowner posts about upgrading from the Broan F40000 that came with their home. Common reasons: too loud, doesn't actually clear cooking smoke, grease collects on cabinets above the stove, mesh filters impossible to keep clean. Multiple owners report that after upgrading to a 600+ CFM hood with baffle filters, they 'didn't realize how bad the old hood was.' Replacement is straightforward — any electrician or handy homeowner.
sources.classification_reason: Owner consensus confirming inadequacy — consistent with professional assessment

sources.snippet: Broan F40000 is UL 507 listed for household electric ranges.
sources.classification_reason: Safety certification — Material Safety report only

bottom_line: Broan-NuTone F40000 is the builder-grade floor — a ~$60 painted steel undercabinet hood with 210 CFM (below the industry minimum of 250 CFM for a 30-inch range), 6.5 sones that discourage use, aluminum mesh filters, and incandescent lighting. Professional consensus: installed because code requires a hood, not because it provides adequate ventilation. Repair techs call it a disposable appliance. It's the cheapest hood a builder can specify and the single most common range hood in American homes. Score reflects that this is a technically functioning ventilation product that fails to adequately perform its primary job.
